questions.q:
The values of $a$ and $b$, for which the system of equations

$2x + 3y + 6z = 8$

$x + 2y + az = 5$

$3x + 5y + 9z = b$

has no solution, are :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given equation is&

$2x + 3y + 6z = 8$

$x + 2y + az = 5$

$3x + 5y + 9z = b$

So,~$D = \left|\begin{cases}2 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & a \\ 3 & 5 & 9\end{cases}\right|$

$= 2 \left(18 - 5a\right) - 3 \left($9 - 3a\right) + $6\left($5 - 6\right)$

$= 36 - 10a - 27 + 9a + 30 - 36$

$= 3 - a$

${D}_{z} = \left|\begin{cases}$2 & 3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & b\end{cases}\right|$

$= 2 \left($2b - 10\right) - 3 \left($b - 15\right) + $8\left($5 - 6\right)$

$= 4b - 20 - 3b + 15 + 40 - 48$

$= b - 13$

The system of equation has no solution if~$D = 0 \text{ and } {D}_{z} \ne 0$

So, If $a = 3, b \ne 13$, then the system of equation has no solution.

questions.q: Let $A$~and $B$~be two~$3 \times 3$~non-zero real matrices such that $AB$& is a zero matrix. Then
options: The system of linear equations& $AX = 0$& has a unique solution
The system of linear equations& $AX = 0$& has infinitely many solutions
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$AB = 0 ⇒ \left|AB\right| = 0$

If~\left|A\right| \ne 0, B = 0$~(not possible)

If~\left|B\right| \ne 0, A = 0$~ (not possible)

Hence~\left|A\right| = \left|B\right| = 0$

So, if~\left|A\right| = \left|B\right| = 0$~then~$A \text{ and } B$~are non-invertible matrix,

So,~$AX = 0$& has infinitely many solutions

questions.q:
If the& system of linear equations,
$x + y + z = 6$
$x + 2y + 3z = 10$
$3x + 2y + \lambdaz = \mu$
has more than two solutions, then $\mu - {\lambda}^{2}$, is equal to.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$x + y + z = 6 . . . \left(1\right)$
$x + 2y + 3z = 10 . . . \left(2\right)$
$3x + 2y + \lambdaz = \mu \ldots \left(3\right)$

From~ \left($1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$,
If $z = 0 ⇒ x + y = 6$ and $x + 2y = 10$,~$⇒ y = 4, x = 2$
If $y = 0 ⇒ x + z = 6$ and $x + 3z = 10$,~$⇒ z = 2, x = 4$

So,~$3x + 2y + \lambdaz = \mu$,~must pass through $( 2,4, 0 )$ and $( 4,0, 2 )$.

$6 + 8 = \mu ⇒ \mu = 14$
And $12 + 2\lambda = \mu ⇒ \lambda = 1$

So, $\mu - {\lambda}^{2} = 14 - 1= 13$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c, d$ be in arithmetic progression with common difference $\lambda$. If~\left|$\begin{cases}x + a - c & x + b & x + a \\ x - 1 & x + c & x + b \\ x - b + d & x + d & x + c\end{cases}$\right| = 2$, then value of ${λ}^{2}$ is equal to________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since,& $a, b, c \text{ and } d$~are in~$A . P .$, therefore

$b - a = c - b = d - c = \lambda$

We have,

\left|$\begin{cases}x + a - c & x + b & x + a \\ x - 1 & x + c & x + b \\ x - b + d & x + d & x + c\end{cases}$\right| = 2$

${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{3}$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}x - 2\lambda & \lambda & x + a \\ x - 1 & \lambda & x + b \\ x + 2\lambda & \lambda & x + c\end{cases}$\right| = 2$

${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{1}, {R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - {R}_{1}$

\left|$\begin{cases}x - 2\lambda & \lambda & x + a \\ 2\lambda - 1 & 0 & b - a \\ 4\lambda & 0 & c - a\end{cases}$\right| = 2$

$⇒ \lambda\left|$\begin{cases}x - 2\lambda & 1 & x + a \\ 2\lambda - 1 & 0 & \lambda \\ 4\lambda & 0 & 2\lambda\end{cases}$\right| = 2$

$⇒ - \lambda\left(4{λ}^{2} - 4{λ}^{2} - 2\lambda\right) = 2$

$⇒ {λ}^{2} = 1$

questions.q: Let for any three distinct consecutive terms $a, b, c$ of an A.P, the lines $ax + by + c = 0$ be concurrent at the point $P$ and $Q ( \alpha, \beta )$ be a point such that the system of equations $x + y + z = 6$, $2x + 5y + \alphaz = \beta$ and $x + 2y + 3z = 4$, has infinitely many solutions. Then $( PQ{)}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$a, b, c$ are in $A . P .$

$⇒ 2b = a + c ⇒ a - 2b + c = 0$

Now, on comparing above equation with $ax + by + c = 0$ we get,

The line $ax + by + c = 0$ passes through fixed point \left(1, - 2\right)$

$∴ P = ( 1, - 2 )$

Now, we know that for infinite solution,

$D = {D}_{1} = {D}_{2} = {D}_{3} = 0$

$D = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & \alpha \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = 8$

And ${D}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}6 & 1 & 1 \\ \beta & 5 & \alpha \\ 4 & 2 & 3\end{cases}$\right| = 0 ⇒ \beta = 6$

So, the point $Q = \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = ( 8, 6 )$

Hence, $PQ^{2} = {7}^{2} + {8}^{2} = 49 + 64 = 113$

$

If the system of linear equations
$2x - 3y = \gamma + 5$
$\alphax + 5y = \beta + 1$, where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in R$~has infinitely many solutions, then the value of \left|9\alpha + 3\beta + 5\gamma\right|$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$2x - 3y = \gamma + 5$

$\alphax + 5y = \beta + 1$

Has infinite many solutions

So,~$\dfrac{α}{2} = \dfrac{5}{- 3} = \dfrac{\beta + 1}{\gamma + 5}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{- 10}{3}, 5\gamma + 25 = - 3\beta - 3$

$⇒ 9\alpha = - 30, 3\beta + 5\gamma = - 28$

Now,~$9\alpha + 3\beta + 5\gamma = - 58$

\left|9\alpha + 3\beta + 5\gamma\right| = 58$

$

questions.q:
Let& $S$~be the set of all integer solutions~ \left(x, y, z\right)$ of the system of equations

$x - 2y + 5z = 0$

$- 2x + 4y + z = 0$

$- 7x + 14y + 9z = 0$

such that $15 \le x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \le 150$. Then, the number of elements in the set~$S$& is equal to ..........

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$x - 2y + 5z = 0 . . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$- 2x + 4y + z = 0 . . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

$- 7x + 14y + 9z = 0 . . . . . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

Applying~$2 \times$~equation~ \left($i\right) +$equation~\left($ii\right)$, we get

$z = 0$

Putting~$z = 0$~in equation~ \left($i\right)$, we get

$x = 2y$

Given~$15 ≤ x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} ≤ 150$

$⇒ 15 ≤ 4y^{2} + y^{2} ≤ 150$

$⇒ 3 ≤ y^{2} ≤ 30$

$⇒ y = \pm2, \pm3, \pm4, \pm5$

$⇒ 8& solutions.

$
